free_it0.label: free-DNA control J39 _000 (as named in task)

pose_tests.note: NU J56 particle poses (54,158 particles); 2D poses/classes from the A1 2D (J45) passthrough

interpretation.verdict: Mostly shorter, with a minority that may be longer. The straight rod that leaves the sfGFP lobe is 65 A from the lobe surface in 3D (NU J56; 63-69 A over a 3x contour range; particle-weighted over the class_3D maps 65 A, range 55-84 A). Free DNA's straight segment is 115 A and a straight 50 bp duplex is 170 A. 3D has no projection foreshortening, so tilt cannot hide length here; this supports H1 for most particles. Every dot-on-rod map also has a weaker, kinked 'far arm' that runs ~100 A from a vertex ~60 A off the lobe, giving a ~150 A path. It joins the lobe density only at contours >= 50-65k A^3. Re-projecting the map at each particle's own pose predicts far-arm mass that the main 2D dot classes (123/130/31/147/103/114/92/145) do not contain: 0.24-1.18 vs 0.00-0.11 of the near-rod mass. Only the long-minority 2D classes 13 and 52 show it, so it is a minority feature or contaminant density, not the bulk conformation. No closed loop or second contact appears at any contour in any map.
interpretation.key_caveat: 45% of the NU/hetero-class-0 particles come from the haze decoy 2D classes 105/12. Hetero refinement did not sort by 2D group (all 4 classes 25-50% dot, 39-56% haze), and class_3D did not either (36-56% haze in every class). Orientation is anisotropic (cFAR 0.17).
